key_insight: The paper proposes a low-cost benchmark, LR-QAOA, that uses mid-circuit measurement and QEC-style connectivity to estimate how quantum hardware handles error-correction primitives at large width and depth.
engineering_relevance: It gives hardware teams a practical pre-logical benchmark for comparing QPUs, diagnosing QEC control flow, and estimating an effective two-qubit depolarizing error rate before full logical-memory tests.
method: Build a QAOA circuit from a code’s check structure so the circuit mirrors syndrome extraction, reset, measurement, and feed-forward patterns.
Track the decay of the approximation ratio r with QAOA depth and convert it into an effective hardware error λ_eff.
Compare direct vs mid-circuit-measurement implementations across multiple QPUs and code families, including surface code, triangular color code, and qLDPC structures.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate the benchmark on 10 QPUs from IBM, IQM, and Quantinuum, with circuits up to 2950 MCM operations and code-structured runs up to 81, 91, and 48 data qubits on Helios-1, H2-1, and ibm_phoenix.
watch_item: Because the metric is indirect and hardware-specific, λ_eff should be interpreted as a benchmark proxy rather than a literal physical error rate.
paper_title: Evaluating the performance of QEC primitives on quantum processors at large width and depth
